summary.text: Laura Murvartian is the Democratic candidate for the Georgia State Senate, District 48, where she faces Republican incumbent Shawn Still in the November 3, 2026 general election.

She is the founder and executive director of Arte GA, a nonprofit that supports Latino professional creatives, and a former corporate executive and small business owner, according to her Ballotpedia survey.

paragraphs.text: Murvartian said in a Ballotpedia survey that she began working at age 12 to help her family and became the first in her family to earn a college degree, a bachelor's in political science with honors from Hamline University in St. Paul, Minnesota.

She received a Woodrow Wilson Fellowship and earned a master's degree in public policy from the University of Michigan, with a focus on international economics; Ballotpedia lists her University of Michigan graduate degree as 1993.

After working at the Federal Reserve she moved to Atlanta, where she served as a corporate executive at several companies and, by her account, as a senior negotiator on information-technology infrastructure and data deals.

She then opened a Georgia wine franchise as its area developer and later founded Arte GA; she is a member of the 2014 Leadership Atlanta class and was named one of the 50 most influential Latinos in Georgia in 2018, according to the survey.
Murvartian was the Democratic nominee for Georgia House of Representatives District 48 in 2024, losing the general election to incumbent Scott Hilton, 54.9% to 45.1%.
In 2026 she won the Democratic primary for Senate District 48, defeating Nathan Hombroek with 63.7% of the vote.
She listed better health care for Georgians, strengthening Georgia's economy and protecting democracy, including voting rights and fair districts, as the key messages of her campaign.
